title: Z, s, and the silent letter ע
why: Three more letters: ז, ס and ע, the second silent letter after א. You learn to point things out and ask with זֶה / זֹאת and מָה זֶה, while discovering that every Hebrew noun has a gender, which you learn along with the word.

{"lessons": ["

Three new letters: ז, ס, ע

LetterNameSound
זzayinz
סsamekhs
עayinsilent, like א

Watch the shapes: ז looks like ו, with a little head that sticks out; ס is rounded at the bottom, while ם is square.

סוּסsus: horse
עִירir: city

Some Israelis pronounce ע from deep in the throat; most don't do anything with it. For you: it's silent.

", "

Two silent letters, two s's

You now know two silent letters: א and ע. They only carry the vowel: אִ and עִ are both read i. Between two vowels, the transliteration marks them with an apostrophe: מִסְעָדָה [mis'ada], restaurant.

For the s sound, there's ס, and another letter you'll see soon: ש with the dot on the left. Another spelling matter!

סַבָּא וְסַבְתָּאgrandpa and grandma [saba ve-savta]

In סַבְתָּא, the ב has no dot: you read savta, not \"sabta\". Israelis call their grandparents saba and savta.

", "

זֶה and זֹאת: this is…

To point something out: זֶה (ze) before a masculine word, זֹאת (zot) before a feminine word. Still no verb \"to be\". To ask, you say מָה זֶה? (what is this?).

זֶה סוּס.This is a horse. [ze sus]
זֹאת מִסְעָדָה.This is a restaurant. [zot mis'ada]

English nouns have no gender, but every Hebrew noun does, so learn it with each word: מִסְעָדָה (restaurant) is feminine, like most words ending in a. And עִיר (city) is feminine, even without a final a.

זֹאת עִיר גְּדוֹלָה.This is a big city. [zot ir gdola]

The dot at the top left of זֹ is a holam: o, as in לֹא.
